newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open slightly higher.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were called to open slightly higher Wednesday in line with LME copper prices overnight after an 1,100 tonne fall in LME warehouse copper stocks to 154,675 tonnes.
COMEX copper stocks rose 1,532 short tons to 45,467 short tons Tuesday.
COMEX May copper was called unchanged to up 0.2 cent from Tuesday's close of 106.25 cents a lb after trading from 106.05 to 106.80 cents in overnight ACCESS trade.
Support is seen around 105.00 cents still, with resistance around 107.50 near a short-term downward sloping trendline since April 4 on the daily charts, traders said.

But daily momentum oscillators remain negative for COMEX May copper, and the contract's five day (weekly) moving average remains below its 21-day (monthly) average and its 55-day (quarterly) average, after retreating from eight-month highs seen in March.
The COMEX May/July spread has eased back to around 1.70 cents in recent weeks also, from around 3.5 cents in March, as tightness in the prompt market has eased.
But overnight, workers at the world's largest copper mine, Escondida, in Chile, voted to strike Friday. Union workers only make up about 15 percent of the staff of 2,000 at the mine though.

Meanwhile, International Wrought Copper Council (IWCC) said copper mine output outside the former Soviet Union and China was expected to rise by five percent this year to almost 9.9 million tonnes, while consumption was only expected to rise three percent in 1997.
